ahead: SHARP_EXPONENT_REVIEW.md confirms all five checked items of SHARP_EXPONENT.md (commit 1abe75b), including its negative claim (section 1.2, the sqrt(N)-interval-length obstruction to the minor-arc quartic at cutoff R) and its positive mechanism (section 2, integrating the Page term over each arc, independently checked by a fresh numerical script matching the source document's own numbers). One defective intermediate equation was found and is non-binding: the term R^2 e^{-(2c/sigma) sqrt(l)(1+o(1))} in SHARP_EXPONENT.md's budget (7), inherited verbatim from MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT.md equation (6), does not follow from squaring MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT.md (5) by the method that document states; correctly derived it should be an R^1 (not R^2) term, itself dominated by the adjacent R e^{-(c/(2 sigma)) sqrt(l)} term and not needing separate listing. This does not change SHARP_EXPONENT.md's boxed (S''') or the exponent constant 2*c_0, and does not change (H''), because the condition this term would induce is strictly weaker than another condition (c_0^2 <= c/16, from the adjacent term) already required by (H''). The same non-binding defect exists in MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT.md (6) itself. MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT_REVIEW.md's earlier check (a-0080/a-0081) did not catch this because its item (4) verified the arithmetic from (6) to its verbal exponent list, not the squaring step from (5) to (6); this is worth a note for anyone revisiting that document, though it is not a wall for this hunt. Separately, I independently re-derived SHARP_EXPONENT.md section 2.1's correction (the real-zero/Page-exceptional distinction) from scratch and confirmed it is right, and that MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT_REVIEW.md item 3's defense of the original (wrong) bullet was itself a miss (it conflated 'no second zero above Page's threshold' with 'no exceptional zero at all for other characters').
